newsitem.title: USA: Infant decapitated by airbag in U.S. accident.
newsitem.headline: Infant decapitated by airbag in U.S. accident.

text.p: A 13-month-old girl riding in a car with her mother was decapitated when a passenger side airbag deployed in a low-speed collision, police said on Wednesday.
"This would otherwise have been a minor damage accident," Lt. Tim Rosenvall of the Boise Police Department said.
The accident that killed Alexandra Greer on Tuesday night came at a time of growing concern about airbag safety and children.

The infant was strapped in a forward facing child car seat. Rosenvall said the airbag hit her head and the impact was so strong that her head was blown through the car's side window. With adults, the impact is usually against the chest which can absorb the force.
The car, driven by the child's mother, 21-year-old Rebecca Blackman, rear ended another vehicle near an intersection close to a shopping mall.
Airbags inflate at up to 200 miles an hour (322 kph) and have been blamed for the deaths of at least 30 children.
Last week federal regulators proposed new rules to allow car airbags to inflate with less explosive force in an effort to reduce the risk of injury to children and to small and frail adults.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has also proposed letting owners disconnect their passenger-side airbag.
